A fitted segmented rating curve, Hodson et al. (2024) parameterisation (S7)

Source: R/flode_classes.R
FlodeSegmentedRating.Rd

The result of rate_optimise_segmented(): a single joint model rather than independent limbs, so @coefficients is one row (C, bp1..bpk, n1..nk, diagnostics), not one row per segment.

Usage

FlodeSegmentedRating(
  gaugings = FlodeEvidence(),
  fit_starts = NULL,
  fit_origin = "independently_fitted",
  lifecycle = "draft",
  schema_version = 2L,
  provenance = list(),
  previous = NULL,
  coefficients = data.table(),
  n_segments = integer(0),
  estimate_breakpoints = logical(0)
)

Arguments

gaugings

A FlodeEvidence table of the observations the fit was built from. A plain data.table with discharge_cms and stage_m columns is accepted and converted by as_flode_evidence(), which generates evidence IDs and records what it assumed. A gauging_datetime column (Date or POSIXct) becomes observation_time and is used for age weighting.

fit_starts

Data.table of multi-start fitting attempts, or NULL if the fit wasn't produced with multi_start = TRUE.

fit_origin

Character. How the fit came to be: one of "independently_fitted", "post_fit_aligned" or "constrained_refit". Read-only @status returns the same value.

lifecycle

Character. Where the rating stands in review: "draft" (default), "under_review", "approved", "superseded" or "withdrawn". The package never sets "approved"; that is a decision for a person.

schema_version

Integer. The layout version the object was made under; see rating_schema_version(). Leave at the default.

provenance

List recording how the fit was made (fitting method, controls, bounds, tool version).

previous

The exact pre-amendment FlodeSegmentedRating this was built from, or NULL (default) for an independently-fitted result. Nothing in the package currently produces an amended FlodeSegmentedRating – this exists for parity with FlodeRating.

coefficients

Single-row data.table: C, bp1..bpk, n1..nk, and fit diagnostics.

n_segments

Integer. Number of segments k.

estimate_breakpoints

Logical. Whether the interior breakpoints were refit as free parameters (TRUE) or held fixed at control (FALSE).

Examples

# Three multiplicative segments, so there is no junction to reconcile.
set.seed(7)
stage_m <- seq(0.3, 3.5, by = 0.05)
discharge_cms <- 4 * pmax(stage_m - 0.1, 0)^1.55 * (pmax(stage_m - 1.6, 0) + 1)^0.9 *
  (pmax(stage_m - 2.4, 0) + 1)^1.1 * exp(rnorm(length(stage_m), sd = 0.03))
fit <- rate_optimise_segmented(discharge_cms, stage_m, control = c(1.6, 2.4))
fit
#> <FlodeSegmentedRating> 3 segment(s), origin: independently_fitted, lifecycle: draft, R² = 0.9994
#>          C        bp1       n1        n2       n3   bp2   bp3  rmse_cms
#>      <num>      <num>    <num>     <num>    <num> <num> <num>     <num>
#> 1: 2.37908 -0.1903062 1.986332 0.7764828 1.051703   1.6   2.4 0.9894296
#>    r_squared n_obs n_starts_attempted n_starts_converged selected_start_id
#>        <num> <int>              <int>              <int>             <int>
#> 1:  0.999443    65                  4                  4                 1
rating_coefficients(fit)[, c("parameter", "estimate", "unit")]
#>    parameter   estimate         unit
#>       <char>      <num>       <char>
#> 1:         C  2.3790801 cms per m^n1
#> 2:       bp1 -0.1903062            m
#> 3:        n1  1.9863320            1
#> 4:       bp2  1.6000000            m
#> 5:        n2  0.7764828            1
#> 6:       bp3  2.4000000            m
#> 7:        n3  1.0517028            1
apply_rating(fit, c(0.5, 1.5, 3))
#>    stage discharge extrapolated
#>    <num>     <num>       <lgcl>
#> 1:   0.5  1.139443        FALSE
#> 2:   1.5  6.748761        FALSE
#> 3:   3.0 77.106058        FALSE
